explain XXXXX in english without using word XXXXX
XXXXX is not a noun. if it is a noun, it is a noun. it's a verb.  so you would use a noun of a noun

a:

in general, you never need to use "an" before a word.  you can, however, have "an an", as in "an apple an apple."

a:

in the us, every country follows a standard.  in fact, at least in the us, most people are not native speakers of english.
the uk, like most of the other countries, uses "an".  however, they only make this a required word in the us, and only in the context of a question, not in the context of a statement.
when referring to the XXXXXs of the uk, for instance, you would use:

"what is the difference between a politician and a XXXXX?"

in the uk, a "gazetteer" or newspaper carries the XXXXX's position on a particular subject.  but in the us, if you are referring to the XXXXXs, you should use "a XXXXX".
